conclusion: The small delegate is a deliberate handoff off the native browser callback, followed by dispatch through the actual Photino UI owner. The downstream InvokeAsync path is not necessarily asynchronous. Removing the task is not a semantics-preserving local optimization. No materially justified alternative survives the assigned source/materiality gate.

actualProducer.behavior: STAThread Main creates one BlazorWindow, registers BasicTestApp.Index once at root, registers two JavaScript-addable component types, then calls mainWindow.Run(). Run navigates and enters PhotinoWindow.WaitForClose().

actualProducer.owner: Existing host document and Blazor WebView boot
actualProducer.behavior: The host loads blazor.webview.js. Boot installs the real JS interop dispatcher, receiver and navigation callbacks and sends AttachPage. The sender serializes supported IPC messages and calls the platform-provided window.external.sendMessage.

Injected window.external.sendMessage forwards to window.chrome.webview.postMessage. The registered ICoreWebView2WebMessageReceivedEventHandler reads the string and directly calls _webMessageReceivedCallback before returning S_OK. There is no intervening managed task in this native producer.
actualProducer.threadContract: The pinned Microsoft WebView2 documentation says the control is created on a UI thread with a message pump and all callbacks occur on that thread.

actualProducer.behavior: Injected sendMessage posts to window.webkit.messageHandlers.Photinointerop. A script-message-received::Photinointerop signal invokes HandleWebMessage, which directly calls the registered callback with the string, then frees the native string and unrefs the JS result.
actualProducer.threadLimit: Signal registration and direct callback chain are established by pinned source. An independent GTK/WebKit callback-affinity contract and a live Linux process were not collected; no universal Linux thread or lifecycle claim is made.

actualProducer.behavior: Injected sendMessage posts to the photinointerop WKScriptMessageHandler. The actual UiDelegate didReceiveScriptMessage method directly calls webMessageReceivedCallback(messageUtf8).
actualProducer.threadLimit: The direct WK callback chain is established by pinned source. An independent WKWebView callback-affinity contract and a live macOS process were not collected.

actualProducer.behavior: The Cdecl string callback is stored in startup parameters as OnWebMessageReceived. That method synchronously invokes WebMessageReceived?.Invoke(this, message). This is the real producer into the sample subscription, not a synthesized callback or unit-test injection.

dispatchOwnership.currentSampleBoundary: For each actual WebMessageReceived event, the sample creates one Task.Factory.StartNew operation with the string as state, CancellationToken.None, TaskCreationOptions.DenyChildAttach and TaskScheduler.Default. The event handler does not await message processing. The comment explicitly says some platforms need to move off the browser UI thread.
dispatchOwnership.baseManager: WebViewManager.MessageReceived performs its source-URI gate and calls _dispatcher.InvokeAsync with asynchronous IPC processing. The returned dispatcher task is discarded. IPC exceptions are reported through IpcSender.NotifyUnhandledException and rethrown inside that task.
dispatchOwnership.sameOwner: BlazorWindow constructs PhotinoDispatcher for its own PhotinoWindow and passes that dispatcher to PhotinoWebViewManager. PageContext passes the same dispatcher to WebViewRenderer; its Dispatcher property returns that owner.
dispatchOwnership.notUnconditionalAsync: PhotinoDispatcher.CheckAccess compares SynchronizationContext.Current with its PhotinoSynchronizationContext and runs the delegate immediately when equal. Otherwise the context may execute synchronously when its queued antecedent is complete. ExecuteSynchronously always uses _window.Invoke and temporarily installs its synchronization context.

nativeInvoke.managed: PhotinoWindow records the constructing managed thread ID. Invoke runs the Action immediately on that thread, otherwise calls Photino_Invoke.
nativeInvoke.Windows: Photino::Invoke posts WM_USER_INVOKE and blocks its caller on a condition variable until the window procedure executes the callback and signals completion.
nativeInvoke.Linux: Photino::Invoke queues gdk_threads_add_idle and blocks its caller until the callback signals completion.

dispatchOwnership.whyNotInline: Calling MessageReceived on the browser callback stack can synchronously enter IPC/application/rendering code through the same-thread native Invoke fast path. The current separate task allows the native event handler to return independently while UI-affine work is forwarded through the platform's marshaling path. A downstream method named InvokeAsync is therefore not proof that the outer handoff is redundant.
dispatchOwnership.reentrancyContract: The pinned WebView2 documentation says callbacks run serially, unsupported nested message loops/modal UI within an event handler can leave the event on the stack, and such work should be scheduled after the event handler completes. This is a contract reason to preserve the boundary, not a reproduced assertion that this unmodified sample currently hangs.
dispatchOwnership.ordering: The current default-scheduler tasks are not documented here as native-arrival FIFO. The synchronization context controls its queued callbacks and continuations. Inlining or adding a new queue would change admission/reentrancy and cannot be called equivalent.
dispatchOwnership.faultAndCancellation: The explicit task scheduler, task exception boundary, DenyChildAttach option, CancellationToken.None and separate discarded dispatcher task are existing behavior. Replacing the task with a direct call or a raw thread-pool work item would require new fault/callback/cancellation equivalence proof; none was fabricated.
dispatchOwnership.lifetime: The window owns the manager and event registration; the event handler and queued task retain the manager/message needed for forwarding. Framework PageContext owns the per-page renderer/service scope and disposes/replaces it on attachment/disposal. This investigation neither adds disposal/cancellation nor claims all post-close callback races are prevented.
